Hi Avery,

Quick follow-up from our privacy team: for the US privacy addendum (CPRA/CCPA posture) we need a clear, itemized deletion SLA matrix that maps types of data we send to which Redwood subprocessors (e.g., logging, telemetry, backups), and the expected time to complete consumer deletion requests (including any dependent third-party flows). - Expected deletion timelines and any conditions that might delay deletion (legal hold, backups)

Emily —

Thanks for the ask. Attached is an initial draft (Deletion_SLA_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a CSV export of our current processor delegation mapping. High level notes up front: 

- Redwood categorizes inbound data as: "Direct request payloads", "KV cache entries", "Telemetry/metrics", "Request logs/diagnostics", and "Embeddings/derived vectors".
- For most customers Redwood acts as a Service Provider (CPRA term) with subprocessors responsible for persistence (object stores), analytics (third-party metrics), and optional backups. We also provide an "operator" variant for private deployments where the customer retains controller-like responsibilities — this changes the mapping.
- Deletion SLAs: standard pipeline deletion for request payloads and embeddings: 30 days (bulk/async removal), telemetry/metrics aggregated: 45 days (retention window + downstream aggregation); logs in backups: up to 90 days depending on backup cadence and retention holds. Exceptions: legal hold or active investigatory hold.

I flagged borderline rows where products or addendum wording may require explicit carve-outs (e.g., prefix caches used for continuous batching that could leave remnants until the next compaction window).

We can walk through in a short call tomorrow — Priyom and Karthik can join to answer infra-level questions.

Best,

Thanks Emily — adding a few infra clarifications inline.

On Mon, Jul 5, 2026 at 12:03 PM avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com wrote:
> I flagged borderline rows where products or addendum wording may require explicit carve-outs (e.g., prefix caches used for continuous batching that could leave remnants until the next compaction window).

Small clarifications from an engineering perspective:
- Continuous KV caches: these are in-memory with optional persistence to object store for cold-start recovery. When persisted, compaction runs daily; logical deletions are applied at compaction time — operationally that means up to ~24 hours for the persisted fragment to be purged after a delete request is accepted. We captured this as a 48-hour window in the spreadsheet to be conservative.
- Backups: nightly snapshots retained for point-in-time restore. We can support targeted deletions from active datasets within 30 days, but full removal from immutable backups will follow the backup retention schedule (we documented 90 days as default, with shorter retention available on request under contract).
- Downstream analytics vendors (list included in CSV): we push only aggregated telemetry by default; if a customer opts into debug logging, raw-ish diagnostics may be sent (we flag this in the matrix).

If Helios needs contractual guarantees shorter than these defaults we can discuss contractual SLAs and an addendum amendment (this typically requires Dedicated or Private deployment terms or a negotiated enterprise commitment).

-Priyom

Tom / Emily —

Appreciate the precise asks. Short answers below and next steps attached.

1) CSV update: we added a column "data_received: raw|aggregated|none" and marked each subprocessor. See updated Processor_Delegation_Matrix.csv in the Drive link (also attached to this thread).

2) Backups: we can support targeted purges from our snapshot store for specific customer IDs as an ad-hoc operational action. Typical lead time is 5–7 business days (manual verification + safe-restore testing). This is not enabled by default due to restore risk; we documented it as an optional contractual SLA (SLA: 7 business days, additional $X per purge request) — if Helios requires included purges we can add it to the addendum but it will likely be scoped into Dedicated or Private pricing.

3) Deletion propagation window: happy to call out a deterministic window. For persisted KV fragments we propose a 48-hour upper bound for deletion propagation to persisted stores (compaction cycle) and 90 days for immutable backup removal unless otherwise contracted. We will include the exact wording we suggest for the addendum in the updated matrix.

Proposed next steps: 
- I uploaded updated Deletion_SLA_matrix_v1.xlsx (marked v1.1) and Processor_Delegation_Matrix.csv to the Drive link and copied the key columns into the attached CSV.
- If helpful, schedule a 20-minute sync tomorrow (suggested: 10:00 AM PT) to walk through the rows Helios legal flagged.
- If Helios confirms the 48-hour propagation and 7-business-day manual purge SLA, we will prepare addendum language options for your counsel to redline.
